entrypoints.summary: The supplied Java harness generates one SunEC EC keypair, repeatedly invokes ECDSA signing on caller-configured curve/hash settings, parses each signature, and emits r, s, and elapsed signing nanoseconds.
Library reproduction instructions direct an operator to run a selected target for a requested signature count, save its output, and pass the observations to the recovery script.

affected_components.role: Measurement harness that invokes SunEC signing and exports timing plus signature observations; it is not historical vulnerable implementation source.
Recovery-workflow driver that selects observations and invokes the imported solver.

negative_controls: No execution transcript in this bundle demonstrates a successful run.
The supplied data documentation notes that timing noise and implementation/platform conditions affect leakage and recovery reliability.
observability.positive_marker: The documented attack workflow identifies reconstructed private-key output as its intended observable end state.

preconditions: The target uses affected SunEC binary-field ECDSA configuration within the disclosed JDK 7–12 scope.
The observer can acquire many signing observations under a common private key and measure or receive signing duration.
The timing signal is sufficiently distinguishable from noise for nonce-bit-length constraints.

trigger_steps.summary: Run the SunEC target with a selected curve, hash algorithm, and requested signature count to emit a signature/timing observation file.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A CSV-like corpus with a key/message header followed by r,s,time rows.
trigger_steps.summary: Provide the collected observation file to the lattice recovery script using matching curve and hash arguments.

impact.affected_asset: The private scalar for the SunEC binary-field ECDSA signing key.
impact.attacker_capability: Collect repeated signatures and timing observations, derive partial nonce constraints, and run the supplied lattice-based recovery workflow.
impact.security_effect: Recovery of the long-term ECDSA private signing key after sufficient timed signing observations.

causal_trace.summary: An observer obtains many ECDSA signatures under one SunEC key together with elapsed signing times. The provided measurement harness records time around signer.sign() and prints parsed r and s values with that elapsed value.

For the evaluated SunEC/OpenJDK/Oracle JDK dataset, signing on sect233r1 with SHA-1 exhibited clear bit-length-only leakage. The mechanism paper attributes this class of timing leakage to scalar multiplication whose loop does not begin at a fixed bit or whose scalar bit length is used to shorten the loop.

ECDSA nonce scalar multiplication has a scalar-bit-length-dependent execution path or iteration count, making signing duration reveal partial information about the fresh nonce rather than leaving it unavailable to the signature observer.

Many timing-derived nonce constraints and ECDSA signature equations can be transformed into a Hidden Number Problem / closest-vector lattice computation to reconstruct the fixed ECDSA private key; the supplied PoC documentation describes observing the reconstructed private key after processing a collected signature file.

failure.operation: ECDSA nonce scalar multiplication during signature generation with bit-length-dependent timing

primary_invariant.statement: Execution of ECDSA nonce scalar multiplication must not expose nonce bit-length information through signing time to an observer collecting signatures.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The evaluated binary-field SunEC dataset is characterized as clear bit-length-only timing leakage, and the paper describes bit-length-dependent scalar-multiplication loop behavior as a leakage source.

raw_refs.role: issue-specific measured SunEC signatures and timings

provenance.source_id: Minerva / CVE-2019-2894 SunEC binary-field ECDSA case

quality.review_notes: Primary paper, measurement harness, SunEC timing corpus, and recovery workflow support the causal chain. The bundle contains no immutable historical OpenJDK scalar-multiplication source, no inspected author patch, and no recorded execution result for this harness. The target harness is measurement/reproduction code, not the vulnerable SunEC implementation. Scope must remain binary-field ECDSA from JDK 7 through JDK 12 and must not be generalized to all JDK ECDSA configurations.

remediation.invariant_restored: Nonce scalar multiplication executes without a nonce-bit-length-dependent timing signal; specifically, a transformed nonce of fixed bit length makes the multiplication loop run the same number of iterations.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Accumulate a sufficiently large set of r,s,time observations under one signing key and supply the saved observation file to the recovery workflow.
data_structure_invariants: Each observation consists of public signature components r and s plus elapsed signing time.
The corpus header supplies public key, message data, and private key for dataset evaluation; the private key is only printed by the harness when its debug property is enabled.

state_context.state_machine: A single generated EC key is initialized for each signing iteration; each iteration signs the same generated message with a fresh ECDSA nonce and records signature components and duration.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: JDK 7 through JDK 12; binary-field-curve ECDSA; disclosure says introduced in JDK 7 and includes JDK 12

oracle.expected_negative: A mitigated implementation should not retain a timing classification correlated with nonce bit length when equivalent repeated signing observations are collected.
oracle.expected_positive: Repeated SunEC signing observations provide r,s,time records whose evaluated SunEC corpus is labeled clear bit-length-only leakage; the documented attack workflow's intended end state is reconstructed private-key output.
